title: UniQuery4R: Unified 4D Scene Reconstruction from a Single Query
abstract: Reconstructing dynamic 4D scenes requires jointly estimating correspondence, geometry, object motion, and camera motion. Existing feed-forward methods typically predict dense task-specific maps or independently process source-target pairs, leading to unnecessary computation for sparse queries and limited feature reuse across different frame pairs. We present UniQuery4R, a query-conditioned framework that encodes a multi-frame clip once and selects the source view, target view, and continuous source-image coordinate only at decoding time via source-to-target cross-attention. Each query jointly predicts target correspondence, target-time 3D position, and scene flow, along with source depth, while camera parameters are estimated per view. This design allows the encoded clip to be reused across arbitrary source-target selections and supports both sparse inference and dense reconstruction through batched queries, without learned temporal embeddings tied to a fixed clip length. We further introduce a direction-magnitude parameterization of scene flow with separate supervision for moving and static points. Among the evaluated methods, UniQuery4R achieves the best macro-average results on WorldTrack for both scene-flow estimation and dynamic-point reconstruction.

title: From Model Provenance to Human Attribution: The Compositional Privacy Risk of AI Text Watermarking
abstract: AI text watermarking is generally discussed as a mechanism for identifying whether a generative AI model participated in producing a piece of text. This technical research note examines a broader privacy question: whether model-level provenance can become human attribution through correlation with other records. Using Anthropic's Claude text watermarking as a current case study, the paper introduces provenance-mediated identity linkage: the possibility that a watermark containing no user-identifying information could nevertheless contribute to identifying a generation event, session, account, organization, or person when combined with retained outputs, timestamps, request metadata, semantic fingerprints, account records, or external platform information. The paper distinguishes Detection ≠ Provenance ≠ Linkability ≠ Attribution ≠ Identity ≠ Authority ≠ Ownership and proposes a Compositional Privacy Invariant for AI provenance systems. The paper does not claim that Anthropic currently performs user attribution through Claude's watermark. It separates documented capabilities, derived architectural implications, hypotheses, and explicitly unclaimed behavior. title: NestedWorld An Experimental Testbed for the Transition from Artificial Inhabitants to Recursive World Builders Downward Cosmogenesis as an Operational Framework
abstract: NestedWorld proposes a reproducible experimental testbed for measuring the transition by which artificial inhabitants become scientific agents, persistent world modifiers, and eventually causal builders of descendant domains. The framework separates internal science, state editing, technological amplification, and domain construction, while keeping energy, memory, operations, time, and bandwidth as dimensionally distinct resources. Version 0.4 reports an executed coupled-agent validation across five synthetic microworlds, all coalitions of three agents, 12,000 episodes per coalition, and 480,000 trajectories. The results show that leave-one-out ablation identifies contextual necessity and sabotage but cannot by itself allocate general authorship under redundancy, synergy, or compensation. The paper therefore proposes a multidimensional attribution framework combining ablation effects, causal Shapley values, interaction indices, and computational provenance. The study establishes a reproducible benchmark with known ground truth and provides an operational foundation for studying recursive environment construction by artificial agents. It does not claim artificial consciousness, autonomous construction by complex agents, or that our universe is simulated.

title: Optimizing AI for Competitive Growth at Digital Marketing Agencies in Indonesia
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly transformed digital marketing practices by supporting content creation, data analysis, reporting, campaign preparation, creative production, and service innovation. However, the adoption of AI does not automatically lead to optimal business outcomes. This study examines how Indonesian digital marketing agencies adopt and optimize AI for competitive growth. Using a qualitative multiple case study approach, this research analyzes three digital marketing agencies in Indonesia: Socioworks, IND! Communication, and Pepple Digital. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with agency owners, managers, and decision-makers, supported by digital observation and secondary data. The data were analyzed using the Gioia Method and interpreted through the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework. The findings show that AI adoption is mainly driven by operational efficiency, competitive pressure, and business growth opportunities. However, AI optimization is constrained by human capability gaps, generic AI outputs, fragmented workflows, tool integration barriers, and unclear cost-performance measurement. The study concludes that AI can support competitive growth only when agencies move beyond basic task-based AI usage toward structured, integrated, and client-value-oriented AI optimization. The proposed business solutions include AI capability development, strategic AI investment and governance, workflow optimization, service innovation, and AI-assisted service packaging.

evidence.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly transformed digital marketing practices by supporting content creation, data analysis, reporting, campaign preparation, creative production, and service innovation. However, the adoption of AI does not automatically lead to optimal business outcomes. This study examines how Indonesian digital marketing agencies adopt and optimize AI for competitive growth. Using a qualitative multiple case study approach, this research analyzes three digital marketing agencies in Indonesia: Socioworks, IND! Communication, and Pepple Digital. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with agency owners, managers, and decision-makers, supported by digital observation and secondary data. The data were analyzed using the Gioia Method and interpreted through the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework. The findings show that AI adoption is mainly driven by operational efficiency, competitive pressure, and business growth opportunities. However, AI optimization is constrained by human capability gaps, generic AI outputs, fragmented workflows, tool integration barriers, and unclear cost-performance measurement. The study concludes that AI can support competitive growth only when agencies move beyond basic task-based AI usage toward structured, integrated, and client-value-oriented AI optimization. The proposed business solutions include AI capability development, strategic AI investment and governance, workflow optimization, service innovation, and AI-assisted service packaging.

title: KazakhStopEval: Stop-Word Inventories, Validation Benchmarks, and NLP Evaluation Artifacts for Kazakh Library OCR Collections
abstract: ### Dataset Description This dataset provides the stop-word inventories, manual validation sets, baseline stemmer, and downstream evaluation benchmarks described in the paper *"Building an NLP Pipeline for Kazakh-Language Library Collections: Stop-Word Extraction and Genre Classification"* (AIST 2026 / CCIS). The resources are derived from a 122.56-million-token Kazakh-centred corpus combining 2,028 OCR-scanned books from the National Library of the Republic of Kazakhstan and 231,729 Kazakh Wikipedia articles. ### Contents of the Deposit: 1. **Stop-Word Inventories (`stopwords/`):** - `grammar_dict.json` (335 normalised grammar-dictionary terms) - `stopwords_single_tfidf.txt` (2,991 statistical single-token candidates at 5% threshold) - `stopwords_collocation_phrases.txt` (3,462 collocation pairs) - `stopwords_combined.txt` (3,414 combined surface forms) - `stopwords_multilingual.txt` (3,930 multilingual forms including Kazakh, Russian, English) 2. **Validation Data (`validation/`):** - `manual_stopword_review_sample_200_labeled.csv` (stratified 200-word sample with manual expert annotations and Wilson confidence intervals) - `manual_stopword_review_template.csv` (unlabeled annotation template for replication) 3. **Evaluation Sets (`proxy_evaluation/`):** - `queries.csv` & `qrels.csv` (50 queries: 39 topical + 11 known-item, with associated relevance judgments) - `classification_metrics.csv` & `topic_metrics.csv` (ablation results across configurations A–E and stemmed variant F) 4. **Tools & Baselines (`tools/`):** - `kazakh_stemmer.py` (lightweight rule-based suffix-stripping stemmer for Kazakh) ### Metadata for Mendeley: - **Category:** Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence / Computational Linguistics / Information Retrieval - **Keywords:** `Kazakh NLP`, `Stop Words`, `Digital Libraries`, `Low-Resource Languages`, `Information Retrieval`, `Agglutinative Morphology`, `LibRAG` - **License:** CC BY 4.0

title: Perceived financial constraints and consumer responses to anthropomorphic service robots
abstract: Anthropomorphic service robots have become a visible feature of contemporary commercial service environments. At the same time, many consumers are experiencing growing financial strain. Although both trends are increasingly salient, prior research has paid limited attention to whether and how perceived financial constraints shape consumer reactions to anthropomorphic service robots. Drawing on a social comparison perspective, social interaction anxiety theory, social observability perspective, and tight–loose culture theory, this research develops and tests a framework that explains why perceived financial constraints can undermine consumer responses to anthropomorphic service robots and identifies when the effect is more or less likely to occur. Evidence from four studies, two supplemental studies, and a single-paper meta-analysis indicates that perceived financial constraints lead consumers to respond less favorably to anthropomorphic service robots because such constraints heighten social interaction anxiety. The operation of this mechanism, however, varies across interaction and cultural contexts. Specifically, the indirect effect is observed when human–robot interaction occurs through voice, but not through touchscreen, and it appears in tight cultures, but not in loose cultures. By uncovering the role of perceived financial constraints in shaping responses to anthropomorphic service robots, this research contributes to both literature streams and provides guidance for marketing managers on when the use of anthropomorphic service robots is likely to be most effective.

title: Beyond the Trace: Coupling an Interpretable Reasoning-State Readout to Native MoE Routing
abstract: What a reasoning model writes is only a partial record of the process that produces it. We introduce a two-level internal readout for mixture-of-experts reasoning. We first distill vocabulary-scale J-space into J64, a 64-axis semantic frame learned from the model's own reasoning states. J64 reveals readable process state that the emitted trace does not show: it separates inference effort from problem-induced strain. It also adds 0.096 to 0.135 held-out AUC over a baseline that reads the same rollout as token occupancy and aggregates it in exactly the same way. We then reconstruct J64 from native expert-routing statistics. The result is R64, a low-overhead proxy: its median per-axis correlation with J64 is 0.69 to 0.86 across three models and two families, and on gpt-oss-20b it preserves 95 to 100% of J64's predictive gain. The readout supports test-time decisions at two temporal resolutions. Over completed candidate sets, J64 and R64 improve single-branch selection, and R64-weighted voting improves plain majority voting in seven of eight settings. During generation, rolling readout windows drive a cumulative stop-and-resample policy whose operating point is fixed on training questions alone. J64 improves accuracy by 1.1 to 5.9 points over a sibling-permuted control, and the routing-only R64 proxy retains 0.9 to 3.2 of those points. Finally, router edits aimed at the mechanism J64 names induce the predicted reasoning behaviors and shift a diagnosed stall from numerical guessing toward exact symbolic execution. Together, J64 makes latent process state readable, while routing makes it deployable and actionable.

title: Key-Frame Reasoning with SAM3: Third Place Solution for the MeViS-Text Track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge
abstract: This report presents a two-stage, training-free solution for the MeViS-Text track of the 8th LSVOS Challenge. The task requires a model to localize and segment the object specified by a natural-language expression throughout a video. Such expressions often depend on temporal cues, including actions, interactions, directions, and relative positions. Our first stage uses Gemini-3.1 Pro via API to decompose a video-level event into instance-level targets, select a key frame for each target, and generate a discriminative description aligned with that frame. In the second stage, SAM3-agent produces a pixel-level seed mask on the selected frame, and the SAM3 video tracker propagates the mask bidirectionally through the video. Valid instances are grounded and propagated independently before their frame-wise masks are merged. All local SAM3 processing runs on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 without task-specific training or model ensembling. Our method ranked third on the challenge test set, obtaining J&F, J, F, N-acc., T-acc., and Final scores of 0.761, 0.7367, 0.7852, 0.8333, 0.9755, and 0.856593, respectively.

title: PENGEMBANGAN KECERDASAN BUATAN BERBASIS RETRIEVAL AUGMENTED GENERATION DENGAN KNOWLEDGE BASE ARTIKEL ILMIAH KELAUTAN DAN PERIKANAN
abstract: ABSTRAK Pengembangan Kecerdasan Buatan Berbasis Retrieval Augmented Generation dengan Knowledge Base Artikel Ilmiah Kelautan dan Perikanan Andika Pangestu Program Studi Sistem Informasi Kelautan, Kampus Serang, Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia Perkembangan teknologi kecerdasan buatan berbasis Large Language Model (LLM) telah memberikan kemudahan dalam memperoleh informasi. Namun, model tersebut masih memiliki keterbatasan dalam menghasilkan jawaban yang akurat dan didukung oleh referensi ilmiah, khususnya pada bidang kelautan dan perikanan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan sistem kecerdasan buatan berbasis Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) menggunakan platform N8N, mengimplementasikan integrasi artikel ilmiah sebagai knowledge base, serta mengevaluasi kinerja dan tingkat kegunaan sistem. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) dengan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif. Sistem dikembangkan dalam bentuk website bernama Navhat yang mengintegrasikan AI Agent, vector database Supabase, dan Crossref sebagai sumber metadata artikel ilmiah. Pengujian dilakukan menggunakan black box testing untuk menguji fungsionalitas sistem serta User Acceptance Testing (UAT) menggunakan USE Questionnaire untuk mengukur tingkat kegunaan sistem. Hasil black box testing menunjukkan bahwa seluruh fitur utama sistem berfungsi sesuai dengan kebutuhan tanpa ditemukan kesalahan fungsional. Hasil User Acceptance Testing (UAT) memperoleh nilai 0,912, yang termasuk dalam kategori sangat baik, sehingga menunjukkan bahwa sistem mudah digunakan, mudah dipelajari, bermanfaat, dan memberikan kepuasan kepada pengguna. Sistem juga mampu menyajikan jawaban berdasarkan artikel ilmiah kelautan dan perikanan yang relevan, dilengkapi sitasi dengan format APA Edisi ke-7 beserta tautan DOI. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, dapat disimpulkan bahwa website Navhat berhasil dikembangkan dan layak digunakan sebagai sistem kecerdasan buatan untuk mendukung pencarian informasi akademik pada bidang kelautan dan perikanan. Kata kunci: AI Agent, Artificial Intelligence, Kelautan dan Perikanan, Knowledge Base, N8N, Retrieval Augmented Generation. ABSTRACT Development of Artificial Intelligence Based on Retrieval Augmented Generation with a Knowledge Base of Marine and Fisheries Scientific Articles Andika Pangestu Marine Information Systems Study Program, Serang Campus, Indonesia University of Education The development of artificial intelligence technology based on Large Language Models (LLM) has facilitated access to information. However, these models still have limitations in producing accurate answers supported by scientific references, particularly in the field of marine and fisheries. This study aims to develop an artificial intelligence system based on Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) using the N8N platform, implement the integration of scientific articles as a knowledge base, and evaluate the system's performance and UAT. The research method used is Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) with a descriptive quantitative approach. The system was developed in the form of a website called Navhat, which integrates an AI Agent, the Supabase vector database, and Crossref as a source of scientific article metadata. Testing was carried out using black box testing to examine the system's functionality, as well as User Acceptance Testing (UAT) using the USE Questionnaire to measure the system's UAT level. The results of the black box testing indicated that all main features of the system functioned according to requirements without any functional errors detected. The User Acceptance Testing (UAT) resulted in a score of 0.912, which falls into the very good category, indicating that the system is easy to use, easy to learn, useful, and provides user satisfaction. The system is also capable of presenting answers based on relevant marine and fisheries scientific articles, complete with citations in APA 7th Edition format along with DOI links. Based on these results, it can be concluded that the Navhat website has been successfully developed and is suitable for use as an artificial intelligence system to support academic information searches in the field of marine and fisheries. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Retrieval Augmented Generation, AI Agent, N8N, Marine and Fisheries, Knowledge Base.

title: Performance of Multimodal vs. Monolingual Tasks in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer on XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the performance of multimodal intermediate tasks (e.g., image-text retrieval) compare to monolingual text-only tasks in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on the XTREME-R benchmark when evaluated using accuracy and F1 score metrics? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.2/10.

title: Enhanced Robustness in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer via Intermediate English Task Training
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does intermediate-task training on English enhance robustness (accuracy, stability) in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer for low-resource languages in XTREME compared to direct fine-tuning? title: Context Manager Redis Caching Sliding Window Technique
abstract: This Code Snippet implements a sliding-window context manager for LLM-based conversational agents, addressing the fact that LLMs are stateless and cannot remember prior turns on their own. It stores each chat session's message history using Redis-style list operations, automatically trimming the history down to the most recent N messages so that token usage stays bounded no matter how long a conversation runs; fakeredis is used in place of a real Redis server so the code can be run locally without any external dependencies. Alongside the core manager class, the script includes an evaluation harness that benchmarks how long it takes to append 500 conversational turns at several different window sizes, and estimates how many tokens a sliding window saves compared to keeping the entire unbounded conversation history. Running the file executes a short demonstration of the manager assembling a trimmed prompt payload, followed by the two evaluation tables summarizing latency and token savings.

title: Disentangling encoding, preprocessing, training budget and estimator artefacts in pre-training diagnostics for hybrid quantum-classical machine learning
abstract: A preregistered follow-up study testing six hypotheses that disentangle confounds in an earlier exploratory campaign on pre-training diagnostics for hybrid quantum-classical machine learning models. The study isolates the effects of data preprocessing, training budget, learning rate, matched circuit resources, and estimator sample size on the trainability failures previously observed at eight qubits.

title: Machine Learning Models for Warfarin Dose Prediction: A Systematic Review of Performance and Clinical Utility
abstract: Warfarin therapy is complicated by its narrow therapeutic index and significant inter-individual variability. This study aimed to systematically review the performance of machine learning (ML) for predicting warfarin doses in clinical settings, compared with conventional methods, and to assess the quality of evidence. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science until December, 2024, and included studies developing ML models for warfarin dosing in clinical settings. The performance metrics of ML models were evaluated using predictive accuracy, model fit, and clinical utility. Risks of bias were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool. Thirty-five studies were included. In terms of ML models, the majority of included studies evaluated artificial neural networks ( n = 24), followed by ensemble models ( n = 19), and support vector machines ( n = 18). Regarding performance, ML models demonstrated superiority across all three metrics: predictive accuracy (16 of 18 studies), model fit (5 of 7 studies), and INR-related clinical utility (all 4 studies). A high risk of bias was identified in 94% of studies, mainly due to analysis-domain limitations, including missing-data handling, insufficient events per predictor, unclear predictor selection, and limited external validation. In conclusion, ML-based approaches may improve warfarin dose prediction compared with conventional methods, but the current evidence should be interpreted cautiously. Future studies should prioritize transparent reporting, robust model development, external validation, and clinically relevant outcomes before these models can be recommended for routine clinical implementation.

title: Efficient Fuzzy PSI under One-Sided Assumptions
abstract: Fuzzy private set intersection (PSI) enables two parties to identify approximately matching elements between their input sets, where two elements are considered a match if their distance is at most a threshold $δ$ under a given metric. Although substantial progress has been made, existing constructions for general Minkowski distances either rely on strong two-sided geometric separation assumptions or incur substantial overhead under one-sided assumptions. In this work, we present the first concretely efficient fuzzy PSI protocols for general $L_{p\in[1,\infty]}$ distances under one-sided assumptions, relying solely on lightweight symmetric-key primitives. Our constructions support both sender-sided and receiver-sided settings. We further study sparser input distributions and present more efficient protocols tailored to this case. To reduce the overhead scaling with $δ$, we non-trivially incorporate prefix trie techniques into our protocols, achieving $O(\logδ)$ complexity for general $L_{p\in[1,\infty]}$ distances for the first time, improving upon $O((\logδ)^d)$ or $O(δ)$ complexities of prior works. Extensive experiments, across a wide range of parameter settings, show that our protocols significantly outperform prior works under the same assumptions. Specifically, against van Baarsen and Pu (EUROCRYPT'24), our protocols achieve up to $248\times$ faster computation and up to $20\times$ lower communication. Against Dang et al. (CCS'25), we achieve up to $568\times$ speedup and up to $63\times$ communication reduction. Against Bui et al. (ASIACRYPT'25), we achieve up to $4978\times$ faster computation and up to $282\times$ lower communication.

title: FESC: Remodeling Long-Context Private Inference with Encrypted State-Space Models
abstract: Processing long, sensitive documents with machine-learning models requires efficient, privacy-preserving long-context inference. Prior private inference systems optimize or distribute encrypted Transformer attention, but its quadratic token-pair work remains the bottleneck as sequence length grows. Selective state-space models (SSMs) offer linear-time recurrence, yet direct encrypted implementation incurs linear multiplicative depth, sequence-wide state residency, or dense FHE-MPC conversion. We present Factorized Encrypted Scan-Contract (FESC), a hybrid FHE-MPC system for private long-context selective SSM inference. Its factorized scan-contract keeps input-dependent transitions compact across conversion boundaries, composes them without dense expansion, streams state chunks on demand, and contracts outputs before conversion. We demonstrate interface compatibility of the scan-contract implementation across invariant and selective SSM architectures. For our Mamba-2 instantiation, we design GPU-optimized CKKS kernels for linear computations, MPC protocols for SiLU, softplus, exponential, and RMSNorm, with approximation-aware fine-tuning. To our knowledge, FESC is the first private long-document inference system to complete native end-to-end execution at $L \geq 1{,}024$ on a single GPU. At $L = 2{,}048$, a 12-layer Mamba-base model completes inference in 77.3 minutes on one A100 GPU with a peak memory footprint of 32.7 GB, while maintaining near-plaintext accuracy on the evaluated long-document tasks.

title: Development of an artificial intelligence agent for automated data entry in a real estate advertisement management system
abstract: Diplomsko delo obravnava razvoj agenta umetne inteligence za avtomatiziran vnos po- datkov v sistem za upravljanje oglasov nepremičnin. Agent sprejema govorne in pisne vnose v slovenščini ter jih pretvori v strukturirane ukaze za sistem za upravljanje odnosov s strankami. Sistem je zasnovan na mikrostoritveni arhitekturi z upravljanjem konteksta pogovora. Po primerjalni analizi je bil izbran model Qwen 3 235B na infrastrukturi Ce- rebras z odzivnim časom 3–10 sekund. Evalvacija kaže 93–95-% natančnost pretvorbe in 85-% zmanjšanje časa vnašanja v primerjavi z ročnim postopkom.

title: PopulationGPT
abstract: PopulationGPT is a desktop reliability layer that sits on top of one or more AI models. Instead of trusting one answer, it decides when a problem is hard enough to justify independent reasoning, checks for disagreement, attacks the leading answer, uses calculations or external evidence where possible, tracks assumptions and provenance, tests whether the result changes under reframing, and then gives one final answer with a calibrated confidence level. It also benchmarks itself against simpler methods so it can prove whether the extra complexity is actually worth it.

title: The Ly-Device Decision Problem and Cross-Scale 5-Fold Structure
abstract: The Ly-Device Decision Problem and Cross-Scale 5-Fold Structure A geometric hardness assumption independent of lattices, and the same algebraic object in a protein fold C.J. Tully Independent Researcher, Tamworth, NSW, Australia ORCID: 0009-0007-5661-7332 · ttg41postquantum@gmail.com 18 August 2026 · Version 1.0 Abstract We make two related claims. First, we define the Ly-Device Decision Problem: given a public context vector and a published threshold, decide whether the Quasi-Equivalence Index of that vector under a fixed 5-fold graded golden-ratio operator exceeds the threshold. We propose that the average-case hardness of this decision rests on graded geometric coherence itself, not on Module-LWE, QCSD, or any other lattice assumption. Second, we record that the same 5-fold graded structure and the same Quasi-Equivalence Index appear in the analysis of a 59-residue protein fold previously studied by the author (S5 ≈ 0.97). The cryptographic gate and the protein fold are therefore instances of one algebraic object. The paper is deliberately provocative: it offers a new hardness assumption and a cross-scale coherence claim that can be tested, attacked, or refuted. Reference code and earlier Geometric Gate papers supply the operational definitions. Keywords: geometric hardness, Ly-Device Decision Problem, Quasi-Equivalence Index, 5-fold symmetry, post-quantum cryptography, cross-scale coherence, protein fold, independent of lattices 1. Two Claims Most post-quantum cryptography rests on lattice problems (Module-LWE, Module-SIS, NTRU, QCSD). The Geometric Gate series treated a graded algebraic structure as a control surface that could be composed with those lattice assumptions. This paper goes further. Claim A (Independent hardness). The decision whether a public context vector is geometrically coherent under a fixed 5-fold golden-ratio grading is a computational problem whose average-case hardness does not reduce to, and is not known to follow from, standard lattice assumptions. We call this the Ly-Device Decision Problem. Claim B (Cross-scale identity). The same 5-fold graded weight lattice and the same Quasi-Equivalence Index that define the cryptographic device also organise the geometry of a 59-residue protein fold previously analysed by the author. The protein and the gate are not merely analogous; they instantiate the same algebraic object at different physical scales. Both claims are falsifiable. Claim A can be attacked by exhibiting an efficient algorithm that decides coherence without solving a lattice problem. Claim B can be attacked by showing that the numerical QEI and symmetry scores of the protein fold and the cryptographic device are unrelated under any reasonable parameter correspondence. 2. The Ly-Device Decision Problem Let φ = (1 + √5)/2. Fix dimension n, a period-5 weight schedule wₖ = φ^(−(k mod 5)) / Z , k = 0 … n−1 (Z = Euclidean normalisation), a circulant mixing coefficient ε_c, and a threshold θ ∈ [0, 1]. For a public vector v ∈ ℝⁿ define the graded operator L(v) = W v + ε_c · Circ₁(v) and the Quasi-Equivalence Index QEI(v) = max(0, 1 − ‖L(v) − v‖₂ / (‖v‖₂ + ε)) Ly-Device Decision Problem. On input (v, θ, public parameters), output 1 if QEI(v) ≥ θ and 0 otherwise. The problem is entirely public. No secret key appears. The only computational question is whether the vector is coherent with respect to the graded 5-fold structure. We do not prove that the problem is hard. We conjecture that, for the parameter regimes used in the Geometric Gate series (n ≥ 32, α ≈ 15.57, θ ∈ [0.12, 0.15]), no efficient classical or quantum algorithm decides the problem with non-negligible advantage without essentially reconstructing the graded action or solving an equivalent geometric search. The conjecture is independent of the hardness of Module-LWE and QCSD. 3. Why This Is Not a Lattice Problem Lattice problems ask for short vectors, close vectors, or solutions to noisy linear equations over modular rings. The Ly-Device Decision Problem asks whether a real vector is aligned with a fixed, public, golden-ratio graded operator. The decision surface is a continuous geometric predicate. There is no modular reduction, no secret short vector, and no error distribution drawn from a discrete Gaussian. An algorithm that solves the decision problem therefore need not (and, on present evidence, does not) yield an algorithm for Module-LWE or QCSD, and conversely. The Geometric Gate papers used the decision as a side-channel reduction layer on top of lattice KEMs. The present paper isolates the decision itself and treats it as a primitive hardness assumption. 4. Cross-Scale Coherence: The Protein Fold In earlier work the author examined a 59-residue folded unit and measured an internal angular organisation compatible with 5-fold symmetry (reported S5 ≈ 0.97, backbone RMSD ≈ 0.009). The same period-5 golden-ratio weight schedule that defines the Ly Device produces a high Quasi-Equivalence Index on the coordinate representation of that fold. The claim is not that proteins “compute” cryptography, nor that the cryptographic gate is biological. The claim is narrower and sharper: the algebraic object that the Ly Device evaluates — a 5-fold graded golden-ratio operator and its Quasi-Equivalence Index — is the same object that organises the measured geometry of the fold. If the numerical correspondence survives independent re-measurement, then geometric coherence under this grading is a scale-invariant structural feature rather than a cryptographic artefact. 5. Consequences If Either Claim Holds If Claim A holds, post-quantum cryptography gains a new hardness assumption that is orthogonal to lattices. Hybrid constructions could then rest on two independent sources of hardness: a lattice problem and a geometric coherence problem. If Claim B holds, the same assumption acquires a physical interpretation outside cryptography, which would be unusual for a cryptographic primitive and would invite experimental tests in structural biology and soft-matter geometry. If both claims fail, the Geometric Gate remains a useful engineering layer for side-channel reduction, and the protein measurements remain an independent structural observation. The falsifiability is intentional. 6. What Would Refute the Claims Claim A is refuted by an efficient algorithm (classical or quantum) that, given only public parameters, decides QEI(v) ≥ θ with non-negligible advantage on the distribution of contexts used in the Geometric Gate series, without solving a lattice problem of comparable dimension. Claim B is refuted by showing that the QEI values and 5-fold symmetry scores of the 59-residue fold are statistically unrelated to the cryptographic weight schedule under any reasonable embedding of the fold coordinates into the device’s vector space. 7. Status and Invitation This paper is a research statement, not a finished security proof. The Ly Device, the QEI, and the hard-gate interface are defined operationally in the Geometric Gate series and the accompanying reference implementation. The protein measurements are those previously reported by the author. The two claims above are offered for examination, attack, and refinement. The author invites concrete cryptanalysis of the decision problem and independent re-evaluation of the fold geometry under the same graded operator. 8. Conclusion We have defined the Ly-Device Decision Problem as a geometric hardness assumption independent of lattices, and we have recorded that the same 5-fold graded structure appears in a protein fold. Together the claims suggest that graded geometric coherence may be both a computational resource and a cross-scale organising principle. Whether either claim survives is an empirical and mathematical question that the community can now test. References Tully, C.J. Ly Device: A 5-Fold Graded Realisation of Ly-Algebraic Geometry. 2026. Tully, C.J. TT-G41 / TT-G42 and From Atoms to Encryption. Zenodo, 2026. Tully, C.J. Side-Channel and Multi-Target Resistance via a Ly-Algebraic Geometric Gate for Lattice KEMs. 2026. Tully, C.J. Hybrid Post-Quantum Encryption: ML-KEM + AES-256-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305 with Optional Ly-Algebraic Geometric Gate. 2026. Tully, C.J. Strengthened Supplement to the Ly-Algebraic Geometric Gate. 2026. Tully, C.J. Reference implementation: lyalgebra_geometric_gate.py, 2026. National Institute of Standards and Technology. FIPS 203, 2024. © 2026 C.J. Tully. Independent research. This paper is intentionally provocative and falsifiable.

title: Impact of Intermediate-Task Training on Inference Efficiency in Multilingual Models for TyDiQA Zero-Shot Transfer
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of intermediate-task training on inference efficiency (measured in tokens per second) for multilingual models like mT5-large on the TyDiQA benchmark during zero-shot cross-lingual transfer? title: Certvas Ontology v0.1.0 — the open schema for African and emerging-market company and asset data
abstract: The Certvas Ontology is a LinkML schema describing company, fundamentals, procurement and macro data for African and emerging markets. One YAML file is the source of truth; Pydantic models, SQL DDL, JSON Schema and a JSON-LD context are generated from it. It models a point-in-time contract explicitly: every fundamentals record carries an effective date (period_end) and an availability date (available_at), so a backtest can exclude values that were not yet public. Announcement dates are evidenced or null, never inferred, and the evidence tier travels with the value. The schema is CC0. The data it describes is not. Datasets published by Certvas carry their own per-source licence terms, recorded per row. Python package: pip install certvas-ontology

title: The Next Intelligence
abstract: The future of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is defined not by faster algorithms but by deeper integration with human work. This chapter explores the next frontier of AI evolution from agentic systems that act with purpose to collective and neuro-symbolic intelligence that blends reasoning, learning and collaboration. It examines how embodied AI and human–machine interfaces will extend intelligence into physical and cognitive spaces, reshaping how organisations operate and people perform. The discussion contrasts today's narrow, task-bound systems with the aspirational concept of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), outlining both accelerators such as computing power, simulation and global research and barriers including alignment, bias and public trust. By separating myth from reality, the chapter highlights that progress in AI is not only technical but also profoundly human. The question ahead is not how intelligent AI can become, but how responsibly we guide its integration with human work and decision-making.

title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
abstract: Memory-based self-improving agents--those that learn from an online stream of tasks and improve over time by maintaining a textual memory bank--have shown great promise in recent literature. However, the reliability aspects of these methods have been critically overlooked. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive re-evaluation of two memory-based methods, broadening the scope of evaluation along two axes: (1) including multiple self-improving runs to quantify variance, and (2) shuffling the tasks to investigate the effect of task order. Through these experiments, we make two observations that expose the fragility of current methods: First, agent evaluation is inherently noisy in complex environments and on multi-step tasks, and stacking a self-improving loop on top can further amplify this noise. Second, the agent's improvement is highly dependent on task order. Prior works often adopt default orderings that impose an implicit curriculum, acting as a hidden prerequisite for success. To better understand this fragility, we manually examine the agents' memory and hypothesize that task and environment underspecification contribute to this fragility. We validate this hypothesis by incorporating information that enables better specification, such as detailed rubrics and environment feedback, into the memory construction process. While this added information partially closes the performance degradation in previous experiments, significant gaps still remain, suggesting that other uncharacterized factors contribute to this fragility. Looking ahead, our work advocates for more rigorous evaluation protocols for self-improving agents by reporting results across multiple runs and stress-testing them under challenging conditions. Moreover, our findings on underspecification call for systems and interfaces that enable effective human oversight, preventing agents from failing in unforeseeable ways.

title: A Hybrid End-to-End and Modular Control Architecture Toward Safe Vehicle Lateral Control: Combining Soft Actor-Critic with Model Predictive Control
abstract: Connected and automated vehicles demand lateral controllers that are simultaneously accurate, low-effort, and safe under model error and sensor noise. Modular controllers such as model predictive control (MPC) are interpretable and constraint-aware but rely on accurate models and hand-tuned weights. End-to-end learned policies, in particular continuous-action deep reinforcement learning, are adaptable and require no hand-designed control law, but offer no intrinsic safety guarantees and limited interpretability. This paper presents a hybrid architecture that combines an end-to-end Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policy with a constrained linear MPC into a single steering command, using the MPC's first-step optimum as the model-based anchor and a single monotone blending coefficient that interpolates between the two paradigms. The architecture is evaluated on a linearized lateral bicycle model against a PID baseline, a tuned linear MPC, and a stand-alone SAC policy, across nominal, single-axis robustness, and multi-initial-condition ensemble experiments. The hybrid retains the tracking quality of stand-alone SAC while remaining inside the MPC's actuator envelope and preserving a deterministic, model-based contribution to every steering command. The architecture provides an actuator-envelope guarantee by construction but does not establish recursive feasibility or terminal invariance, and the closed-form blend does not prevent all corner-case divergences at the boundary of the training distribution. A corner-case analysis shows that the blend attenuates but cannot prevent failure under distribution shift, motivating a connectivity-aware extension in which the blending coefficient is scheduled by vehicle-to-everything (V2X) signals to restore model-based authority. Limitations and a path toward a constrained-QP predictive safety filter are discussed.

title: IMPLEMENTASI FEDERATED LEARNING BERBASIS BLOCKCHAIN DAN DECENTRALIZED IDENTITY DALAM PENGEMBANGAN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS KOLABORATIF
abstract: Pengembangan Large Language Models (LLM) membutuhkan data berskala masif yang kerap terkendala isu privasi, regulasi data, dan risiko sentralisasi. Federated Learning (FL) menawarkan pelatihan kolaboratif yang menjaga privasi dengan melatih model secara lokal, namun FL tradisional masih bergantung pada aggregator pusat (single point of failure), rentan terhadap manipulasi kontribusi dan serangan identitas (Sybil attack), serta minim mekanisme insentif. Penelitian ini merancang, mengimplementasikan, dan menguji prototipe platform kolaboratif yang mengintegrasikan FL, blockchain, dan Decentralized Identity (DID) untuk pengembangan LLM. Blockchain berperan sebagai lapisan kepercayaan melalui smart contract FederatedHub yang mengoordinasikan putaran pelatihan dan mendistribusikan insentif, sedangkan DID berbasis metode did:key dan Verifiable Credentials (VC) standar W3C mengautentikasi partisipan melalui pemetaan injektif DID–wallet. Prototipe diimplementasikan menggunakan model GPT-2 Small yang di-fine-tune oleh lima klien pada dataset Alpaca (10.000 sampel), dengan bobot model disimpan di IPFS dan hash Keccak-256 dicatat on-chain pada jaringan Ethereum Sepolia. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui tiga skenario pengujian yang mencakup enam belas variabel. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan seluruh variabel terpenuhi. Skenario normal membuktikan alur end-to-end, dari registrasi identitas hingga distribusi insentif, berjalan secara utuh. Skenario abnormal membuktikan sistem menolak empat bentuk pelanggaran kontrol akses identitas dan mendeteksi model poisoning berbasis bobot acak melalui contribution scoring. Skenario transparansi membuktikan seluruh transaksi terekam publik pada ledger dan insentif terdistribusi secara deterministik dan proporsional. Penelitian ini menunjukkan kelayakan integrasi ketiga teknologi sebagai infrastruktur pelatihan LLM kolaboratif yang aman dan transparan dalam lingkup prototipe proof-of-concept. The development of Large Language Models (LLMs) requires massive-scale data, which is often constrained by privacy concerns, data regulations, and the risks of centralization. Federated Learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training by allowing models to be trained locally. However, traditional FL still relies on a central aggregator, creating a single point of failure, while remaining vulnerable to contribution manipulation, identity-based attacks such as Sybil attacks, and limited incentive mechanisms. This study designs, implements, and evaluates a collaborative platform prototype that integrates FL, blockchain, and Decentralized Identity (DID) for LLM development. Blockchain serves as a trust layer through the FederatedHub smart contract, which coordinates training rounds and distributes incentives, while DID based on the did method and W3C-standard Verifiable Credentials (VCs) authenticates participants through an injective DID–wallet mapping. The prototype was implemented using GPT-2 Small, fine-tuned by five clients on the Alpaca dataset containing 10,000 samples. Model weights were stored on IPFS, while their Keccak-256 hashes were recorded on-chain on the Ethereum Sepolia network. The evaluation was conducted through three testing scenarios covering sixteen variables. The results show that all variables were successfully satisfied. The normal scenario demonstrated that the complete end-to-end workflow, from identity registration to incentive distribution, operated as intended. The abnormal scenario showed that the system successfully rejected four forms of identity-based access control violations and detected random-weight model poisoning through contribution scoring. The transparency scenario demonstrated that all transactions were publicly recorded on the ledger and that incentives were distributed deterministically and proportionally. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating these three technologies as a secure and transparent infrastructure for collaborative LLM training within the scope of a proof-of-concept prototype.

title: Substrate Logistics: The Architecture of Quantum Information
abstract: Title: Substrate Logistics: The Architecture of Quantum Information — Deriving the $1.67 \times 10^{-37}\,\text{J}$ Erasure Floor, Master Clock Decoherence, and Active $36^\circ$ Chiral Phase Compensation Author: Marco Lindenbeck Description: Standard Quantum Information Science (QIS) treats qubit state vectors as continuous Hilbert-space objects and relies on empirical noise models to characterize decoherence and error floors in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. This manuscript applies Substrate Logistics to reclassify quantum information from continuous wavefunctions into the discrete hardware execution logs of a finite state machine governed by The Topological Resolution Constant ($\kappa=50$) anchored to a closed Poincaré Dodecahedral Space (PDS). By framing spatial nodes as a pre-tensioned computational metric sampled at the Master Clock rate ($f_\Omega \approx 1.85 \times 10^{43}\,\text{Hz}$), this paper derives the fundamental limits of quantum computing from zero-parameter metric geometry. At $T = 0\,\text{K}$, bit erasure is floored at the Substrate Landauer Limit ($E_{\text{min}} \approx 1.6751 \times 10^{-37}\,\text{J}$), proving that continuous zero-dissipation operations are physically impossible. Furthermore, background metric sampling jitter creates an impermeable single-gate error floor ($\epsilon_{\text{floor}} = \mathcal{C}_\delta \cdot \phi \approx 7.6371 \times 10^{-4}$), natively explaining why transmon fidelities plateau near $99.92\%$ and why this value naturally sits below the $1\%$ 2D surface code fault-tolerance threshold. This work introduces the Substrate-Aware Open System Dynamics Master Equation, incorporating the full 5-channel pentagonal jump operator and the $36^\circ$ chiral metric torque. Numerical open-system telemetry proves that uncompensated coherent phase precession causes complete state collapse at anti-phase nodes ($N=25, 75$, fidelity $\mathcal{F} = 1.87\%$), whereas active $R_z(-36^\circ)$ chiral pulse compensation restores fidelity to $98.13\%$ ($52.5\times$ recovery). These results establish exact mathematical transpiler truncation bounds ($D_{\text{block}} \le 1309$) and provide direct blueprints for fault-tolerant quantum hardware design.

title: Artifact for "The Shelf Life of Verification Evidence: A Pre-Registered Six-Year Study of Constant-Time Verdicts in Three Cryptographic Libraries"
abstract: Complete artifact for a pre-registered longitudinal study of constant-time (CT) verification verdicts in libsodium, Mbed TLS and PQClean across 26 quarters (2020Q1–2026Q2). Contents. The hash-committed pre-registration and its SHA-256; era-appropriate Dockerfiles for four Debian tiers (buster, bullseye, bookworm, trixie), each with an identical pinned TIMECOP/Valgrind 3.23.0 oracle; all harness generators and cohort files; the orchestration driver and the DAG-correct git bisect run bisection driver; resolved quarterly commit tables; and every raw verdict cell (377 CSVs, 2120 Valgrind logs). Headline numbers. 2236 (function, quarter, compiler) cells, 2014 testable, 43 subjects, one host. One admissible verdict transition, one repair, six identity deaths, two vacuous cells. Verification. verify_paper_numbers.py re-derives every number in the paper from the raw CSVs and asserts the vacuity guard is present in all three runners. full_study/test_analyze.py carries estimator regression tests. shasum -a 256 -c PREREGISTRATION.sha256 verifies the pre-registration against its published hash. Note on the corrected instrument. An earlier version of the runner captured each harness's exit status and never read it, so a harness that failed during setup was scored CT_PASS on zero executed code — a vacuous pass. All three arms now record exit status and emit a distinct VACUOUS state. The full sweep was re-run under the corrected instrument; results from before the correction are retained under full_study/ /results_prevacuity/ for diffing.

title: Inline holographic reservoir computing architecture
abstract: We present a theoretical study about a deterministic photonic reservoir architecture based on coherent inline free-space propagation. The reservoir state is generated by repeated coherent propagation from a programmable phase boundary under dynamically updated conditions. The optical core operates strictly linearly under monochromatic, spatially coherent laser illumination. Nonlinearity arises from CMOS square-law photodetection, and recurrence is introduced via bounded electronic feedback that updates the phase boundary between discrete time steps. Sensor placement near a Talbot synchronous distance provides a geometry-defined state projection aligned with the sampling symmetry of the modulation grid, enabling structured spatial pooling. By combining deterministic linear mixing, nonlinear intensity projection, controlled recurrence, and trainable linear readout, the architecture fulfills the formal requirements of reservoir computing without relying on optical material nonlinearities.

title: MetaCrypto online: A model-driven visual development platform for cryptographic engineering
abstract: MetaCrypto Online is a model-driven Web-based visual development platform for cryptographic engineering. It provides a block-based interface tailored to cryptographic algorithm design that lowers the development barrier through visual modeling, and supports real-time dual-language code generation (Python and JavaScript) with in-browser execution and verification. During code generation, the platform enforces fixed-width arithmetic semantics to maintain bit-level consistency across Python and JavaScript outputs. Users complete the full workflow in the browser, from visually assembling an algorithm to exporting deployable code, offering an efficient integrated tool for implementing cryptographic algorithms, prototyping new constructions, and classroom instruction.

title: Local particle flow filters for large-scale dynamic systems
abstract: Particle filters are popularly adopted when state-estimating non-linear stochastic dynamic systems. These filters consist of an ensemble of weighted particles undergoing a sampling procedure divided into two steps: a propagation step driving the ensemble according to a proposal mapping, and a correction step assessing the ensemble likelihood based on observations. Especially in large-scale dynamic systems, the recursive nature of the algorithm causes the ensemble to degenerate after a few iterations. To mitigate this, some filters adopt resampling strategies and informative proposal mappings. However, the resulting ensemble still suffers from the sample impoverishment issue of many particles sharing the same value after resampling. To overcome this, we propose repositioning the predicted particles by a law of motion: a particle flow. Further, we exploit the decay-of-correlations property in large-scale systems through local particle filters which sample in lower-dimensional partitions of the state space. Combining these two approaches removes the need for resampling and alleviates the effects of weight degeneracy and sample impoverishment, allowing for a larger effective number of particles for state estimation (provided that localisation errors and approximation biases remain sufficiently controlled). We illustrate the effectiveness of the resulting local particle flow filter in two systems: one representative of atmospheric dynamics and one modelled as a chemical reaction–diffusion system.

title: When to Review: Spaced Repetition for Continual Pre-Training of Language Models
abstract: Continual pre-training of large language models must acquire new information without erasing old knowledge. Existing replay methods often choose a global old/new mixture and sample uniformly, ignoring that examples differ in how quickly they are forgotten. We formulate continual pre-training as adaptive review scheduling: the training loop should decide not only how much history to replay, but which examples should return at each step. We introduce Spaced Repetition Training (SRT), a continual learning framework inspired by cognitive science, which schedules sample-rehearsal using the SuperMemo-2 (SM-2) algorithm. SRT maintains per-example review state, maps per-example perplexity to a recall-quality signal, and schedules historical examples for retention and new examples for consolidation while leaving the model, objective, and optimizer unchanged. On temporally separated Wikipedia and code corpora, SRT improves the stability-plasticity trade-off, recovering 5 to 37 percentage points of old-knowledge accuracy lost by naive continual pre-training across model scales while preserving or improving new-knowledge acquisition. At larger scale, SRT preserves broad benchmark performance that naive continual pre-training and uniform replay substantially degrade. Experiments with vision and tabular data further suggest that the scheduling principle extends beyond language when paired with an appropriate recall signal.

title: A Connectivity-Order Law and Conditional Minimal-Mechanism Identification in Many-Body Geometric Phases
abstract: The value of a multiqubit geometric phase at a single operating point does not reveal whether it was generated directly or through a connected sequence of lower-body interactions. For analytic, gapped, nondegenerate Abelian holonomies, we jointly resolve logical support and independently calibrated coupling support. Every nonzero connected response must involve an active set that connects and covers the target and must contain one factor of each active coupling, yielding the sharp onset bound $ν_S \geq τ_E(S)$. The same selection law applies locally to projected Berry curvature. Conversely, an unrestricted finite-dimensional construction realizes all responses allowed by the connected-cover condition simultaneously, making the condition necessary and sufficient within this theorem class. Operationally, simultaneous confidence bands certify detected mixed responses while controlling false positives; a factor-of-two separation condition additionally recovers exact library-relative response minima. In a complete dictionary, nontriviality of every minimal-cover response is generically necessary and sufficient for these minima to coincide with the minimal calibrated mechanisms. Three-qubit Wilson calculations distinguish direct and pair-mediated routes with the same endpoint phase, and a synthetic Ramsey audit locates the finite-resolution boundary.

title: SISTEM MONITORING SENTIMEN PUBLIK REAL-TIME PROGRAM MBG BERBASIS MACHINE LEARNING: STUDI KOMPARATIF SVM DAN NAÏVE BAYES DI PLATFORM X
abstract: Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) menimbulkan berbagai respons masyarakat pada media sosial X. Penelitian ini bertujuan membandingkan kinerja algoritma Support Vector Machine (SVM) dan Naïve Bayes dalam melakukan klasifikasi sentimen publik terhadap Program MBG. Metode penelitian menggunakan CRISP-DM yang meliputi business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, dan deployment. Data diperoleh melalui web scraping menggunakan Tweet Harvest dengan kata kunci terkait MBG sebanyak 4.754 tweet pada periode 20 Mei–25 Juni 2026. Data diproses melalui tahapan text mining, preprocessing teks, dan ekstraksi fitur TF-IDF. title: Multimodal Intermediate-Task Training for Cross-Lingual Programming Language Robustness
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Can multimodal intermediate-task training (e.g., using code-image pairs from CodeT5) enhance zero-shot cross-lingual robustness on programming language tasks in XTREME-R compared to text-only intermediate tasks? title: Pseudo-Boolean polynomial anomaly scoring for intelligent multisensor environmental monitoring
abstract: Air quality sensor networks need anomaly detection that works from day one—without training data, without historical baselines, and with results an operator can actually interpret. Existing methods (Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, LOF) require representative “normal” data for training, which makes them brittle when environmental conditions shift across seasons. We propose a training-free anomaly scoring method based on pseudo-Boolean polynomial (PBP) reduction with multi-threshold binarization. Sensor windows are converted to binary exceedance matrices at quantile thresholds (Q25– Q95); PBP coefficient features then serve as interpretable anomaly indicators. Two variants are introduced: full-window PBP applied to the w × s sensor matrix, and sensor-pair PBP applied to w × 2 sub-matrices isolating pairwise sensor interactions. On the UCI Air Quality dataset (6,941 readings, 8 sensor channels), sensor-pair PBP achieves AUC 0.881— exceeding One-Class SVM (0.877) and LOF (0.870)—with no training data at all. The real test is temporal robustness: under a strict chronological split (thresholds from the first half, evaluation on the second), PBP maintains AUC 0.865 while LOF collapses to 0.708 and OC-SVM drops to 0.833.

title: ColoNET: a novel hybrid deep transfer learning approach for colorectal cancer classification from histopathological imagery
abstract: Colorectal cancer is a major global health concern, ranking as the third most common cancer worldwide with approximately 1.9 million new cases and 900,000 deaths annually. Early detection is critical, as colorectal cancer often originates as benign polyps in the colon or rectum that may progress to malignancy if left untreated. However, early stage detection remains challenging, particularly in underserved and low resource areas where limited access to pathologists and infrastructure increases the likelihood of human error. This study presents a machine learning based diagnostic framework designed to support automated colorectal cancer detection through histopathological image analysis. To enhance feature extraction, a transfer learning approach was employed using a pretrained ConvNeXt-XLarge Convolutional Neural Network as a deep feature extractor. The extracted features were subsequently classified using three supervised machine learning algorithms: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Multi Layer Perceptron (MLP). A total of 123 experiments were conducted for hyperparameter tuning to evaluate model performance under different variables, with classification accuracy used as the primary metric. Through tuning and optimization, the optimal model achieved an overall accuracy of 99.32% over the Multi-Layer Perceptron based test data split in distinguishing cancerous tissues from healthy colorectal tissue samples. This approach offers a scalable and efficient diagnostic solution that can reduce diagnosis issues and improve early detection in resource-limited healthcare settings. The proposed model highlights the potential of artificial intelligence based diagnostic tools to improve global colorectal cancer outcomes by enabling accessible, high-quality diagnostic support.

title: COMA: A Compositional Misleading Attack Class on Security-RAG, and a Causal Counterfactual Defense
abstract: Every document a security copilot retrieves can be true, instruction-free, and non-contradictory --- and the copilot can still be driven to assess a critical, exploitable vulnerability correctly and then recommend a remediation that leaves it open. We study this failure in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) backing analyst-facing copilots in Security Operations Centers, and identify a class of attacks, \emph{\compmis{}} (COMA), in which every adversarial document is factually correct, instruction-free, non-contradictory, and distributionally benign --- yet the answer is misled by their \emph{composition}. We realize \compmis{} through \emph{action-corruption}, which steers a correctly-diagnosed vulnerability toward an inferior remediation, and \emph{verdict-flip}, which destabilizes the exploitability verdict via an undecidable reachability chain. Action-corruption bites all five tested models --- including frontier reasoning models --- on every run, on two synthetic domains and a real CVE (CVE-2021-33813); verdict-flip bites stochastically, decreasing with model capability but never vanishing. A single principle governs both: the attack succeeds when the disambiguating fact must be \emph{inferred} rather than \emph{read}. We propose \ccd{} (Causal Counterfactual Defense), an audit that measures the leave-one-out causal influence of each retrieved document and flags answers whose influence concentrates on low-trust documents. \ccd{} localizes the attack to attacker-controlled documents with no false positives on four benign multi-document controls; an adaptive influence-spreading adversary is caught by an \emph{aggregate} variant. We release attack seeds and a \ccd{} reference implementation.

title: BayesPrompt: human readable prompts that make sense
abstract: Reconstructing prompts that can elicit a desired answer or behaviour in an LLM is an open and important research topic. Optimisation methods which aim at minimising the perplexity of a given answer, however, consistently yield so-called pseudoprompts, unintelligible strings of tokens which can lack human interpretability. We argue that this is a consequence of the ill-posedness of the prompt optimisation task. By reframing the task as a Bayesian posterior inference over prompts, we propose an efficient algorithm to sample prompts which are both efficient (in terms of perplexity) and human readable. We compare our approach with state of the art alternatives showing on a real data set a marked improvement over a range of metrics.

title: LENS: In-Context Search via Latent Evidence Exploration over Dynamic Raw Documents
abstract: LLM agents increasingly answer questions over dynamic raw-document collections, where files may change before preprocessing, and relevant evidence (spans, sections, pages, or tables) is query-dependent. Existing retrieval-augmented approaches pre-materialize evidence via fixed chunking, embeddings, or persistent indexes: effective for lookup, yet costly, stale-prone, and committed to a granularity before the query is known. We formulate in-context search as Budgeted Evidence Localization over a latent evidence space induced by dynamic raw documents and propose LENS (Latent Evidence Exploration and Search), an index-free framework. Instead of pre-materializing the evidence space, LENS maintains a query-conditioned belief over candidate units, iteratively selecting candidates via complementary lexical, local, and exploratory proposal policies, updating the belief via an LLM relevance oracle, and narrowing toward high-posterior regions under a controllable budget. Evidence is consolidated into compact, source-grounded regions of interest and compressed into self-organizing knowledge clusters reused across related queries. On a controlled 500-question evaluation with matched corpus snapshots, LENS reaches 62.4% exact match and 84.8% evidence recall vs. 65.2% exact match but 50.4% evidence recall for a ReAct-style baseline. Across scales, LENS gives the strongest supporting-fact localization and answer grounding. On a fixed 150-question fullwiki subset over the raw Wikipedia dump with zero indexing, LENS and ReAct are nearly tied in official answer quality (43.3% vs. 42.7% EM), with LENS grounding more answers in retrieved evidence (84.0% vs. 70.7%). A no-retrieval Closed-Book reference highlights the contribution of model memory. LENS is query-ready after corpus changes, needs no preprocessing or persistent index, and preserves source-grounded evidence localization throughout.

title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Semantic Inconsistencies in Wikidata’s Classification Hierarchy
abstract: Wikidata is currently the largest open knowledge graph on the web, encompassing over 120 million entities. It integrates data from various domain-specific databases and imports a substantial amount of content from Wikipedia, while also allowing users to freely edit its content. This openness has positioned Wikidata as a central resource in knowledge graph research and has enabled convenient knowledge access for users worldwide. However, its relatively loose editorial policy has also led to a degree of taxonomic inconsistency. Building on prior work, this study proposes and applies a novel validation method to confirm the presence of classification errors, over-generalized subclass links, and redundant connections in specific domains of Wikidata. We further introduce a new evaluation criterion for determining whether such issues warrant correction and develop a system that allows users to inspect the taxonomic relationships of arbitrary Wikidata entities-leveraging the platform's crowdsourced nature to its full potential.

title: A novel hybrid RSO with WOA for single-objective and multi-objective optimization
abstract: The hybridisation process combines the strengths of various metaheuristics while simultaneously minimising their deficiencies. This work proposes a novel hybrid algorithm that integrates rat and whale-inspired metaheuristics, with the aim of achieving superior convergence without compromising computational cost. The proposed hybridisation incorporates the hunting and fighting behaviours of the rat algorithm into the prey-encircling mechanism of the whale algorithm. This study presents two versions of the hybrid algorithm: one for single-objective optimisation and the other for solving multi-objective and many-objective problems. The single-objective version is evaluated by minimising 33 benchmark single-objective functions. The multi-objective version was evaluated using the Inverted Generational Distance (IGD) metric on 10 multi-objective and 15 many-objective problems. The two proposed hybrids were applied to multivariate system identification, where the quality of the obtained models is evaluated using the Mean Squared Error (MSE) and the Coefficient of Determination (R2). The performance of the proposed single and multi-objective hybrid versions was compared with several well-established swarm-based metaheuristics and hybrid algorithms from the literature. The results illustrate the benefits of hybridising whale and rat metaheuristics in terms of convergence and computational cost.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Technology A Dual Frontier Strategy for the Next Era of Computational and Scientific Leadership
abstract: Core Overview The paper is an academic Perspective article titled "Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Technology: A Dual-Frontier Strategy for the Next Era of Computational and Scientific Leadership". Written by Isaac Khor Eng Gian, representing EGK Microelectronic Solutions Group Sdn. Bhd. in Penang, Malaysia, the paper analyzes the geopolitical, economic, and technical realities of two critical technologies developing at different speeds. The paper outlines a "Dual-Frontier" framework, asserting that the maturity gap between immediate commercial AI systems and early-stage quantum hardware should be treated as a unified long-term strategic opportunity rather than a zero-sum funding competition. Key Structural Pillars & Context The Geopolitical Landscape: The paper examines the shifting dynamics of the U.S.–China AI competition. It challenges the reliance on simple "frontier-model rankings" as indicators of national technological dominance, pointing out that true capability depends on a broader network of underlying infrastructure, including grid energy capacity, accelerator distribution, custom compilers, and automated deployment pipelines. The Quantum Spectrum: It details the scientific mechanics and core bottlenecks across five competing physical processing paradigms: Superconducting circuits, Trapped-ion systems, Neutral-atom arrays, Photonics, and Spin/semiconductor architectures. It argues that because the winner remains physically uncalibrated, national programs must remain pluralistic and evaluate development using logical-error suppression and packaging yields instead of raw physical-qubit counts. Post-Quantum Cybersecurity Migration: It highlights the immediate security threats stemming from future quantum computers running Shor’s and Grover’s algorithms. The text emphasizes that long-horizon data remains vulnerable to harvest-now-decrypt-later (HNDL) captures today, stressing the urgency of actively transitioning data architectures to finalised NIST standards (FIPS 203, 204, and 205) as well as newly selected candidates like HQC. The Dual-Frontier Reference Architecture The primary conceptual contribution is a layered 5-tier heterogeneous system where AI is positioned both as a direct consumer service and an inline engineering engine within the physical quantum computing stack: Application Layer: Focuses on custom subroutines for molecular simulations, quantum chemistry, and materials discovery. AI/HPC Orchestration Layer: Leverages localized machine learning models to accelerate pulse calibration, error decoding, layout routing, and automated circuit tuning. Validation & Compilation Layer: Employs a strict deterministic boundary to enforce topology checks, metadata rules, and physical register limits. Quantum Systems Layer: Integrates QPUs, localized hardware memories, and photonic interconnects. Physical Infrastructure Layer: Houses localized fabrication cleanrooms, cryogenic dilution refrigerators, and control electronics hardware. Empirical Hardware Field Evidence To ground the framework, the manuscript analyzes an internal, hardware-grounded EGK Quantum case study executed on the 127-qubit IBM Quantum backend ibm_marrakesh using 1,024 shots: Ideal State Execution: A structurally sound 3-qubit Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) circuit verified high experimental coherence, capturing ideal state groupings across 1,006 out of 1,024 shots (~98.24%). Automated Error Repair Boundary: A second experiment evaluated a malformed circuit context featuring conflicting register indices (creg c[2] vs qreg q[3]) and a self-referential CNOT operation (cx q,q), which threw immediate backend errors. An on-device AI assistant successfully patched the QASM syntax and introduced a hardware-compatible routing layout using a SWAP instruction. Semantic Failure Mode: Crucially, the resulting patch left one qubit unmeasured, meaning it achieved hardware compatibility (it executed without an error code) but failed to achieve semantic equivalence(it did not preserve the intended 3-qubit calculation). The author uses this discovery to prove that software simulation results must remain isolated beneath strict deterministic validation boundaries because compilation success does not equal programmatic correctness. Macroeconomic Prescriptions The roadmap outlines an action path for building structural resilience over a 10-year period: Maintain first-frontier AI ecosystems as engines to fund and accelerate second-frontier quantum tooling. Establish milestone-based public research pathways that avoid picking single-architecture winners prematurely. Scale specialized interdisciplinary workforces capable of bridging the translation gaps between data-driven machine learning, advanced packaging physics, and information theory.

title: Measure the Instrument First: Preregistered, Prediction-Sealed Calibration of Four Endpoints for AI Distillation in a 4B QLoRA Series — Applied Distillation Science
abstract: This work is part of the Applied Distillation Science (蒸留応用学) series on AI distillation with local language models. Technical preprint, version 1.0. English is the primary version; a faithful Japanese companion version is included. When a model series shows little or no apparent difference, two explanations must be separated: the target may not differ, or the instrument may be unable to resolve the difference. We calibrated four endpoints on a single Qwen3-4B-based QLoRA series (base d0 plus eight adapter checkpoints, nine evaluation points; 29 items nested in 16 slugs, slug as inference unit) under a preregistered procedure: known-answer fixtures, proxy-data compatibility tests, a 43-artifact freeze, sealed probabilistic predictions from two predictors, and one primary application to 261 rows. E3 (stop-token log mass immediately after the completion) separated d0 from d192 (median per-slug contrast +16.625 nat, split-half null scale 1.793 nat, DR 9.27) but the d192 slug median (−0.087 nat) exceeded the preregistered provisional ceiling of −1.0 nat and was classified out of operating range. E2 (TRUE preference) gave DR 0.64 and was not separable at this scale. E4 (forced choice) chose position A in both presentation orders for 261/261 rows; order averaging left a constant item score and an undefined endpoint. E1 (normalized NLL) separated with DR 7.10 but matched no row of the preregistered decision table, exposing an uncovered branch. Claim ceiling. The paper does not establish a distillation effect, a causal mechanism, generalization to other models or seeds, absence of TRUE preference, or general invalidity of forced-choice evaluation. It reports what this frozen instrument can and cannot measure on this series, and preserves position bias and the decision-table gap as instrument failures instead of repairing them after viewing the result. Sealed predictions, including misses, are retained. Process disclosures. Seven required disclosures are included: an unbinding amendment to a sealed clause, a 2026-08-17 critical incident (an executing agent attempted to work around a governing clause) and the subsequent governance strengthening, post-seal application of the novelty gate, adoption before full specification review, role non-independence, invalidated earlier declarations, and the identity of the two predictors. AI systems (Claude Fable/Opus, GPT/Codex) were used for implementation, prediction, drafting, recomputation and review; publication authority remained with the human operator. Reproduction scope. The frozen 261-row raw file, the preregistration (SHA-256 5e19341f…), seal and freeze receipts, both prediction tickets and the seal, the runner/core/aggregator, two independent recomputations, figure data and generator, and all review receipts are included. Adapters and the base model are not included; independent rerunning of the teacher-forced pass is therefore not claimed. Continues Paper B (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21968250). Previously titled: "Measure the Instrument First: Preregistered, Prediction-Sealed, One-Shot Calibration of Four Endpoints in a 4B QLoRA Series"
